headline_findings: A single arm-worn IMU can do the core job for free-weight and bodyweight movements: RecoFit (Microsoft Research, CHI 2014; final study 114 participants / 146 sessions) reported >95% precision and recall for finding exercise periods, 99% / 98% / 96% recognition on circuits of 4 / 7 / 13 exercises, and rep counts accurate to ±1 [verified: Morris et al. 2014, https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2556288.2557116].

Commodity wrist devices reach the same envelope on closed exercise sets: MiLift (IEEE TMC 2018, 22 users, COTS smartwatch) gives >90% precision/recall for weightlifting session detection and type classification with a median rep-count error of 1.12 reps on a median 9.65-rep set; MM-Fit (IMWUT 2020) reaches 94% exercise-recognition accuracy from the smartwatch alone (96% multimodal, 85% phone-only, 82% earbud-only) on unseen subjects over 10 exercises [verified: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8118128/ ; https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3432701].

Wrist-only sensing measurably degrades on leg-dominant work: in WEAR (IMWUT 2024, 18 outdoor workout activities, 50 Hz on both wrists and ankles) the right-wrist-only inertial F1 fell to 58-67 versus 68-77 with the right ankle added, and mAP fell as low as 28-35 for DeepConvLSTM-class models versus 47-61 with wrist+ankle; the authors state wrist-only data 'significantly decreases predictive performance across all algorithms and metrics' [verified: Bock et al. supplementary Table 9, https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3699776].

Field validation of commercial wrist apps is weaker than lab papers: the Apple Watch / StrengthControl study (Sensors 2021; 30 trained athletes, 363 sets of squat, bench and deadlift at 60-80% 1RM) recognised the correct lift in 88.4% of sets and counted reps without significant error only for back squat (p=0.68) and deadlift (p=0.09) [verified: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8471343/].

Load cannot be sensed by an IMU and bar velocity is only validated for bar-mounted sensors: a 2021 systematic review (22 studies, 8 IMU models) found 7 models valid and reliable versus linear transducers, Vmaxpro gives ICC 0.91-0.96 with limits of agreement <0.12 m/s, but GymAware remained most valid and Beast Sensor / Bar Sensei least valid in the back squat and power clean; no wrist-band velocity validation was found, so weight must come from the FitForge prescription or user entry [verified: PMC8038306, PMC8431394, PMC7404723].

In-sensor inference for a small closed set is a microamp-class solved problem: STMicroelectronics ships a wristband 'gym activity recognition' decision tree (~30 nodes, 3-s windows of 26-30 Hz accelerometer data, classes none / bicep curls / lateral raises / squats) that runs inside the LSM6DSOX / LSM6DSV80X, with MLC overhead of about 3.1 µA in a comparable example, and Bosch's BHI260AP 'Klio' learns a repetitive pattern on-sensor and emits a float repetition count [verified: ST and Bosch Sensortec GitHub sources].

Streaming raw IMU to the phone is trivial for BLE: 6-axis int16 at 50 Hz is 600 B/s (4.8 kbps), under 0.4% of the 1,504 kbps Nordic measures with LE 2M PHY and 251-byte data length, so the on-device vs phone vs batch decision is about battery, latency and privacy, not bandwidth [estimate from verified Nordic sample output, https://github.com/nrfconnect/sdk-nrf/blob/main/samples/bluetooth/throughput/README.rst].

Self-supervised pretraining is the state of the art for label-scarce personalisation: fine-tuning a UK-Biobank-pretrained wrist model lifted PAMAP2 F1 from 0.605 to 0.789 and WISDM from 0.684 to 0.810 (npj Digital Medicine 2024), and LIMU-BERT-X runs 7.5 billion on-device predictions per day for 500,000 couriers at >90% accuracy after pretraining on 1.43 million hours of IMU data (MobiCom 2025) [verified: https://github.com/OxWearables/ssl-wearables ; https://github.com/WANDS-HKUST/LIMU-BERT_Experience].

Prior-informed recognition has direct academic precedents (process-instruction priors for factory HAR, IMWUT 2019; sensor-context zero-shot HAR, AAAI 2025; few-shot transfer and on-device few-shot personalisation on RecGym, 2025; metric-based few-shot rep counting reporting about 0.7 reps/set MAE, 2024), which supports a plan-aware, one-set-per-exercise calibration design [secondary: titles verified via curated survey list, several numbers not re-verified].

WHOOP sleep staging is validated but modest: versus polysomnography, 2-stage agreement 89% (sleep sensitivity 95%, wake specificity 51%, kappa 0.49) and 4-stage agreement 64% (kappa 0.47) in the WHOOP-sponsored Miller 2020 study; WHOOP-AUTO 86% / 63% (2021); a 2025 six-device PSG study including WHOOP 4.0 found >90% sleep sensitivity but only 29-52% wake specificity across devices [verified: tandfonline 10.1080/02640414.2020.1797448 ; PMC8226553 ; SLEEP Advances zpaf021].

Not found this session: numeric PPG heart-rate accuracy during resistance training for WHOOP / Apple Watch / Polar Verity Sense, and WHOOP HRV / resting-HR validation figures; the web-search budget was exhausted and PubMed, PMC, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref and Europe PMC are egress-blocked, so these are recorded as open questions with candidate papers rather than guessed [not found].

Design conclusion: an upper-arm or forearm band (the RecoFit / MyoGym placement, in the Polar Verity Sense form factor which already streams 52 Hz accelerometer + gyro and 55 Hz PPG with offline recording) running a plan-aware, per-user-calibrated counter is the technically de-risked path; leg-press / machine-only work should stay user-confirmed unless a second (ankle/pocket) sensor is added [estimate synthesised from the verified sources above].

data_points.note: Numeric rows not extracted. Implication: do not go below ~50 Hz for the recognition stream; ST's 26-30 Hz in-sensor example is for a 3-class problem.

data_points.metric: STMicroelectronics in-sensor gym activity recognition (Machine Learning Core) configuration
data_points.value: LSM6DSOX: accel-only ±8 g at 26 Hz ultra-low-power, IIR1 low-pass, 4 features (mean, peak-to-peak, min, max) on 3-s windows (78 samples), one ~30-node decision tree; classes: no activity, bicep curls, lateral raises, squats; separate left/right-wrist configs. LSM6DSV80X variant: 30 Hz, 90-sample windows
data_points.source_title: STMicroelectronics STMems_Machine_Learning_Core - application example 'Gym activity recognition'
data_points.note: Repository discontinued July 2025 in favour of github.com/STMicroelectronics/st-mems-machine-learning-core. Accuracy of the example is not published in the README; it demonstrates feasibility, not performance.

data_points.metric: Machine Learning Core current overhead (in-sensor inference)
data_points.value: 3.1 µA additional for MLC (ASM330LHHX tow-detection example, 12.5 Hz); ~20 µA total device current for LSM6DSV16X asset-tracking example
data_points.source_title: STMicroelectronics STMems_Machine_Learning_Core application examples (Tow detection; asset tracking READMEs)
data_points.note: Figures are for non-gym examples; the gym example's own current is not stated. Order of magnitude: in-sensor decision trees are effectively free compared with a radio link or an MCU neural network.

data_points.metric: Bosch BHI260AP 'Klio' on-sensor self-learning repetition recognition
data_points.value: learns a repetitive-motion pattern on-sensor (learning progress 0-100, interrupted by non-repetitive or insignificant movement); recognition output = activity index + float repetition count; tunable recognition responsiveness (approximate number of cycles before recognition), sensitivity, learning speed, similarity threshold, max patterns; pattern-similarity scoring API
data_points.source_title: Bosch Sensortec BHY2-Sensor-API (bhy2_klio_defs.h, bhy2_klio.h, examples/klio_selflearning)
data_points.note: Commercial proof that 'record one set to calibrate, then count' can run in a sensor-hub with no phone in the loop. Accuracy figures not published in the repo.

data_points.metric: nRF5340 SoC compute

data_points.metric: Measured BLE throughput (Nordic sample output)
data_points.value: 1,504 kbps (3,762,990 bytes in 20.003 s; peer received 7,602 GATT writes at 1,524,771 bps)
data_points.source_title: nRF Connect SDK sample: Bluetooth Throughput (README sample output)
data_points.note: LE 2M PHY, data length 251 bytes, nRF54L DK pair, connection interval 320 units. Default BLE parameters (23-byte MTU, 27-byte packets, 1M PHY) give far less but still orders of magnitude above an IMU stream.

data_points.metric: Raw IMU stream bandwidth and per-session volume
data_points.value: 6-axis int16 at 50 Hz = 600 B/s = 4.8 kbps (100 Hz: 9.6 kbps; 9-axis 100 Hz: 14.4 kbps); a 60-min session = 2.16 MB at 50 Hz or 4.32 MB at 100 Hz
data_points.source_title: Arithmetic from sensor format (6 axes x 2 bytes x rate) - own calculation
data_points.note: Under 0.4% of the measured 1,504 kbps link; a whole session fits in a few MB of on-band flash for later sync. Conclusion: bandwidth never decides the architecture.

# Rep-detection science: can one band do the core job?

## 0. Method and coverage caveats

WebSearch delivered 14 queries before the session budget (200/200) was exhausted; WebFetch and curl were egress-blocked for every scholarly host tried (PubMed, PMC, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref, Europe PMC, DBLP, MDPI, Zenodo, GitHub Pages). The only open channels were raw.githubusercontent.com and anonymous git clone, so a second tier of root sources was pulled from author- and vendor-maintained repositories: the RecoFit dataset repo (Microsoft), the WEAR repo including its 27-page IMWUT supplementary PDF (text-extracted locally), the MM-Fit starter repo, the RecGym site source, LIMU-BERT / LIMU-BERT-X, IMU2CLIP, OxWearables ssl-wearables, HAR-Bench, the STMicroelectronics Machine Learning Core examples, the Bosch BHY2 (BHI260AP) sensor API, Polar's official BLE SDK docs, Zephyr board and sample docs, and Nordic's throughput sample. Every number below carries its confidence tag; items that could not be reached are listed as not found, not guessed.

## 1. Landmark systems

**RecoFit (Morris, Saponas, Guillory, Kelner; CHI 2014).** One arm-worn accelerometer + gyroscope at 50 Hz. Three sub-problems: find exercise periods (>95% precision/recall), recognise the exercise (99% / 98% / 96% on circuits of 4 / 7 / 13 exercises), count reps (accurate to ±1). The public dataset holds >200 participants (2.5 GB). The system already embodies the plan-aware insight: accuracy is a function of the candidate-set size. [verified]

**MiLift (Shen, Ho, Srivastava; IEEE TMC 2018).** Commercial smartwatch, automatic segmentation, machine and free-weight lifts, 22 users: >90% average precision/recall for session detection and type classification; median rep error 1.12 on a median 9.65-rep set. [verified]

**MM-Fit (Strömbäck, Huang, Radu; IMWUT 2020).** 10 exercises, two TicWatch Pro (100 Hz), two phones (210 / 500 Hz), an eSense earbud (90 Hz), RGB-D video and pose; set boundaries and rep counts annotated. Multimodal 96%, watch-only 94%, phone-only 85%, earbud-only 82% on unseen subjects. [verified]

**MyoGym (Koskimäki, Siirtola 2017).** Forearm Myo armband, 30 exercises x 10 reps, 10 subjects, IMU + 8-channel EMG at 50 Hz; a 2024 CNN-ResBiGRU reports 97.29% accuracy / 92.68% F1 with EMG + IMU. [secondary]

**RecGym (2022).** Wrist, pocket and calf units at 20 Hz with IMU + body-capacitance, 12 classes including LegPress, LegCurl and Adductor machines, ~50 h. It is the benchmark for the 2025 on-device few-shot personalisation paper. [verified]

**WEAR (Bock, Kuehne, Van Laerhoven, Moeller; IMWUT 2024).** 22 participants, 18 outdoor workout activities, four Bangle.js watches (both wrists and ankles, 50 Hz, ±8 g) plus head camera; 1,137 minutes. Best inertial-only F1 86.20 (DeepConvLSTM, 1-s windows) and mAP 88.36 (ActionFormer); camera-only F1 72.49; fused F1 86.98 / mAP 93.12. Licence CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial). [verified]

**Self-supervised / foundation models.** LIMU-BERT (SenSys 2021) introduced BERT-style masked reconstruction on 20 Hz IMU windows; its successor LIMU-BERT-X was pretrained on 1.43 M hours from 60K subjects and 1.1K phone models and runs 7.5 billion on-device predictions/day for 500K couriers at >90% accuracy (MobiCom 2025). OxWearables' UK-Biobank model (npj Digital Medicine 2024) lifts PAMAP2 F1 from 0.605 to 0.789 and WISDM from 0.684 to 0.810 when fully fine-tuned. IMU2CLIP (Meta, EMNLP 2023) aligns Ego4D head-IMU with CLIP video/text. The 2024-2026 wave (RelCon at Apple, LSM / LSM-2 / SensorLM at Google, PRIMUS, CrossHAR, MoPFormer, MASTER, Inertia-1, WHAR Arena, TransfHAR) is catalogued in the Awesome-IMU-Sensing survey; their numbers were not retrievable. [verified for repos; secondary for the list]

## 2. Reported accuracies and the placement question

The robust pattern across sources: on a closed set of 4-13 upper-body or whole-body movements a single wrist/arm IMU gives 94-99% recognition and ±1-rep counting; open-world sets of 18-30 classes drop to F1 in the 80s and, for a wrist-only sensor, into the 60s. WEAR's ablation is the cleanest placement evidence: right-wrist-only F1 61.97 / mAP 29.56 versus 73.54 / 49.49 with the right ankle added and 75.44 / 59.14 with all four sensors (DeepConvLSTM, 1 s). The temporal-action-localisation models show the same wrist-only penalty (TriDet F1 63.62 -> 74.91). The authors conclude wrist-only data 'significantly decreases predictive performance' and that the ankle recovers most of it. [verified]

What fails from a wrist: leg-dominant work with a quiet upper body (leg press, leg curl, adductor; on WEAR the lower-body drills), static holds (no periodic signal to count), and machine exercises where the wrist path is short and constrained. The Apple Watch study makes the point at product level: 88.4% lift recognition on only three barbell lifts, rep counts acceptable for squat and deadlift but not bench press. [verified] A multi-IMU study reports 0.83 (right wrist) -> 0.88 (both wrists) -> 0.91 (+back) accuracy. [secondary] Frequency matters: WEAR's models degrade at 25 and 10 Hz, so a recognition stream should stay at ~50 Hz even though ST's 3-class in-sensor example runs at 26-30 Hz. [verified]

Placement recommendation for lifting: upper forearm / upper arm (RecoFit, MyoGym, Polar Verity Sense placement) sees the same arm kinematics as a wrist but is less affected by wrist flexion and grip artefacts and, for PPG, is a better optical site than the wrist during gripping. If leg-machine coverage matters, the evidence says add a second sensor low on the body, not a second wrist. PAMAP2 (wrist + chest + ankle) and RecGym (wrist + pocket + calf) exist precisely because one site is not enough for open-world sets.

## 3. Load and velocity

No IMU measures load. Bar velocity is measurable by bar-mounted IMUs: the 2021 systematic review (22 studies, 8 models) rated 7 as valid and reliable versus linear transducers; Vmaxpro shows ICC 0.91-0.96 with LoA < 0.12 m/s; GymAware (linear transducer) remains the most valid in squat and power clean while the wearable-style Beast Sensor and Bar Sensei were least valid. An Apple Watch VBT paper exists (2023) but its numbers were not captured. Conclusion: weight must be user-entered or taken from the FitForge prescription; the band can at most flag rep-to-rep slowdown (proxy for proximity to failure) from its own arm kinematics, which should be labelled as a trend, not a velocity measurement. [verified]

## 4. On-device inference vs streaming vs batching

**Bandwidth is a non-issue.** 6-axis int16 at 50 Hz is 600 B/s (4.8 kbps); at 100 Hz, 9.6 kbps. Nordic's throughput sample measures 1,504 kbps with LE 2M PHY and 251-byte packets. A 60-minute session is 2.16-4.32 MB, which fits in a few MB of on-band flash. [verified sample output; estimate for arithmetic]

**In-sensor (µA class).** ST's MLC runs a ~30-node decision tree on 3-s windows of 26-30 Hz accelerometer features inside the LSM6DSOX / LSM6DSV80X for a 4-class gym example (none / bicep curls / lateral raises / squats), with MLC overhead of about 3.1 µA in a comparable example and ~20 µA whole-device budgets in asset-tracking examples. Bosch's BHI260AP Klio learns a repetitive pattern on the sensor hub (progress 0-100), then outputs an activity index plus a float repetition count, with tunable responsiveness (number of cycles before recognition) and pattern-similarity scoring. Neither vendor publishes accuracy. [verified]

**MCU neural nets (mA class while active).** Zephyr's TFLite-Micro magic_wand runs a 20 KB accelerometer gesture model; Edge Impulse's standalone inferencing example targets nRF52832 / nRF52840 / nRF5340 / nRF54L15 and Thingy:53 with CMSIS-DSP/NN; the nRF5340 application core is a Cortex-M33F at 128 MHz. Per-inference latency and current figures were not retrievable (vendor docs blocked); treat this as an open question to be settled on a devkit. [verified capabilities; latency not found]

**Phone-side.** LIMU-BERT-X proves lightweight transformer-family models run at national scale on phones. FitForge's static-export PWA can run a TFLite / ONNX-web model, but the Capacitor iOS shell would be needed for background BLE.

**Recommended split.** Band: sample IMU at 50-100 Hz, run a cheap in-sensor or MCU 'is this a set?' detector and a peak-based counter, store raw windows for the flagged sets, and stream compact set summaries (start, end, count, feature vector) live; upload raw windows after the session for model improvement only with explicit consent, matching FitForge's rule that health data never syncs silently. Phone: run the plan-aware classifier and reconcile with the workout player. This keeps radio duty cycle low, keeps raw data local by default, and makes the live-count experience robust to BLE drop-outs.

## 5. The plan-aware recogniser

FitForge knows the next exercise, the target reps and the prescribed load. The band therefore solves a verification problem, not open-world recognition: confirm that the motion matches the expected exercise (or one of the few plausible alternatives), segment the set, count reps. RecoFit's own numbers (99% at 4 candidates vs 96% at 13) and the LNCS 2023 wristband study (98% on 4 exercises, MAE < 0.2) show how much easier the small-candidate regime is. Academic precedents for using a prior: process-instruction-informed factory HAR (IMWUT 2019), sensor-context zero-shot HAR (ZeroHAR, AAAI 2025), timestamp-supervised segmentation (TMC 2024). Personalisation precedents: domain-adaptive batch-norm incremental personalisation (IMWUT 2020), few-shot transfer (TIST 2025; TS2ACT IMWUT 2024), on-device few-shot personalisation evaluated on RecGym (arXiv 2508.15413, 2025), metric-based few-shot rep counting for unseen exercises reporting ~0.7 reps/set MAE and 74% exact sets (arXiv 2410.00407; attribution to be confirmed). Bosch Klio is the commercial embodiment of 'record one set, then count'. [secondary for numbers; verified for titles and APIs]

Product design that follows: (1) first-time calibration set per exercise, stored as a per-user template; (2) template matching plus a small pretrained encoder (ssl-wearables or LIMU-BERT-style) fine-tuned on FitForge's own logs, because WEAR is non-commercial and RecoFit's licence is unreviewed; (3) every confirmed set in the app is a free label, so the model improves with use; (4) exercises the wrist/arm sensor cannot see (leg machines, isometrics) stay tap-to-confirm.

## 6. Physiological tracking science

Sleep: WHOOP vs PSG (Miller 2020, WHOOP-funded position): 2-stage agreement 89%, sleep sensitivity 95%, wake specificity 51%, kappa 0.49; 4-stage agreement 64%, kappa 0.47. WHOOP-AUTO (2021): sleep sensitivity 90%, wake 60%, agreement 86% / 63%. The 2025 six-device PSG study including WHOOP 4.0: >90% sleep sensitivity but only 29-52% wake specificity. A 2024 JMIR systematic review (Fitbit Charge 4, Garmin Vivosmart 4, WHOOP) consolidates this. Implication for the readiness engine: total sleep time is systematically overestimated on fragmented nights and stage minutes are low-precision; use them as coarse inputs with wide priors. [verified]

Heart rate / HRV during lifting: not found this session. Candidate references to verify: Boudreaux et al. 2018 (MSSE, wearables during cyclic and resistance exercise), Bellenger et al. 2021 (Sensors, WHOOP HR/HRV vs ECG), Polar Verity Sense / OH1 validation papers. The mechanism is not in doubt: wrist PPG degrades under grip-induced motion and perfusion changes; the Polar Verity Sense form factor (upper-arm band, PPG 55 Hz, ACC/gyro 52 Hz, offline recording) is the industry answer and doubles as the IMU placement recommended above. [not found for numbers; verified for Polar specs]

## 8. Bottom line for the band

One upper-arm band can reliably confirm and count the upper-body and compound free-weight sets that make up most of a FitForge plan, provided the recogniser is plan-aware and per-user calibrated; it cannot see leg-machine work or isometrics, cannot measure load, and should not claim bar velocity. Physiological tracking from the same site is credible for sleep/RHR trends with known biases and needs its own validation for HR during lifting.
open_questions: Numeric PPG heart-rate accuracy during resistance training for WHOOP 4.0/5.0, Apple Watch and Polar Verity Sense (MAE / MAPE / ICC vs chest ECG) - not found; verify Boudreaux et al. 2018 (Med Sci Sports Exerc), Polar Verity Sense / OH1 validation studies, and any 2023-2026 lifting-specific PPG validations.
WHOOP HRV (RMSSD) and resting-HR validation against ECG (Bellenger et al. 2021, Sensors) - bias and limits of agreement not retrieved.
Per-device WHOOP 4.0 stage-level kappa and specificity in the 2025 SLEEP Advances six-device study, and the pooled estimates in the 2024 JMIR systematic review.
The exact RecoFit sensor placement (forearm vs upper arm) and the '93% of sets within ±1 rep' figure quoted in the brief - abstract only says 'accurate to ±1'; confirm from the CHI 2014 PDF.
Wrist-only vs upper-arm-only head-to-head for gym lifts: WEAR compares wrist vs wrist+ankle, MyoGym is forearm-only; no paper found that isolates upper-arm vs wrist on the same lifts.
On-device latency and current per inference for a ~20-100 KB IMU classifier on nRF52840 / nRF5340 (Edge Impulse and Nordic benchmark pages were egress-blocked) - measure on a devkit.
Accuracy of ST MLC gym example and Bosch Klio rep counting - vendors publish configuration but no validation numbers.
Quantitative gains of on-device few-shot personalisation on RecGym (arXiv 2508.15413) and of metric-based few-shot rep counting (arXiv 2410.00407) - figures not verified against the PDFs.
Licence terms of the RecoFit and MM-Fit datasets for commercial model training (WEAR is confirmed CC BY-NC-SA, non-commercial).
Whether a wrist/arm IMU can produce a usable proximity-to-failure signal (rep-velocity decay within a set) - no validation study found; would need in-house data against a linear transducer.

Whether static holds (planks, isometrics) and machine-based leg exercises can be detected from an arm band at all, or should remain tap-to-confirm; RecGym's LegPress / LegCurl / Adductor classes are the test set.

The unattributed search-summary claims 'MAPE 3.5% for exercises with device rotation vs 31.0% without; MAE 0.0-4.6 reps; inter-device ICC > 0.770' could not be pinned to a paper and were excluded from data_points.
